qualification: All-source retention is a conservative hot-buffer screen, not inherited99% capture in thin receivers.
Constant k,cp,rho are requirements/scenarios; no high-temperature damage property law or coupled radiative-cooling/vapor model.
Photon grey flash and finite-depth spectral proxies remain separately identified; a grey luminosity does not determine an escaping spectrum.

The bulk-mode bound is valid for periodic stage streams with constant mean pickup. One-day separation between large pulses is an explicit dispatch requirement; arbitrary burst schedules can require more storage.

A positive back-face delay kernel maps the bulk-mode history to the pickup temperature with constant offset minus qmean*L/(2*k). Raising the bulk floor by that offset keeps pickup at least1000K without fixing its temperature.
A one-day bounded dispatch lateness relative to nominal stage release times adds at most qmean*86400/(Sigma*cp) to the summed bulk storage range; this is an explicit schedule acceptance sensitivity.
Free plate curvature uses a selected constant thermal-expansion coefficient5e-6/K. This is a thermal-strain/segmentation screen, not a fatigue/joint or irradiated-material qualification.
No fixed1000K back-face or instantaneous peak heat-engine capacity is assumed.
